title: Turned Square
subtitle: Rigid, and fitted to its node
description: A square turned forty-one degrees: the angle a report named when a turned node came out squashed.

The turn is a pure rotation of the shape's own definition, and the turned outline is then fitted to the node with one uniform scale -- the same factor on both axes -- so nothing is cut off at the node's edge and nothing is stretched to make it fit. A square at 45 degrees becomes the largest diamond the node holds; at 41 it is that diamond a little off true.

The shape this replaced sampled its own pixels inside the node's square, so a shape that filled its node -- which every one of them does -- lost its corners to the node's edge at any angle. That is what the squashed nodes were.
